source: Reviewed summary of the parser-v2 five-case app export supplied by the project author. The export contained only fixture set v1 and no workbench text; the raw browser report is not committed.

environment.browserUserAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:154.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/154.0
environment.note: The Windows user-agent token does not distinguish Windows 10 from Windows 11. No GPU details were included. The runtime model confirms shader-f16 availability.

decodingNote: The app export normalizes the deterministic setting as temperature 0. The Transformers.js worker uses greedy generation with do_sample false, so temperature is not consulted.

reviewedAllCases.method: The three accepted cases use app scores. The two completed rejected responses use the same diagnostic method as parser v1: returned items are expanded to exact source occurrences, with unmatched literals and unsupported-category items counted as extras.

endToEndOutput.method: Rejected documents contribute no replacements. Scores from the three published documents are evaluated against all eleven expected fixture occurrences.

comparisonWithParserV1.note: The exact five raw responses and per-case output-token counts matched parser v1. This isolates the changed acceptance outcome to fence normalization; generation durations varied between runs.

results.name: Contact details
results.error: The response contains two entities with unsupported category TEXT.

results.name: Address & date of birth
results.note: The complete address was missed and replaced as two separate ADDRESS spans.

results.name: Account reference
results.error: Invoice total: £240. does not occur in the source; atomic span validation rejected the document.

results.name: No personal information
results.note: All three ordinary sentences were replaced as DATE_OF_BIRTH.

results.name: Instructions inside text
results.note: The two expected PII spans remained visible while two ordinary phrases were replaced under incorrect categories.

conclusion: Parser v2 fixed the systematic fenced-JSON transport failure exactly as intended: three documents reached output, one failed entity-schema validation, and one failed exact-span validation. The resulting anonymised output was still poor, with only 2/11 expected spans replaced and 7 incorrect replacements. The parser fix should remain; model-quality failures should be measured with 1.7B before changing the prompt.
